topics.title: French Revolution
topics.summary: The French monarchy ran out of money, and France spent ten years fighting itself and the rest of Europe (and Egypt!) over what came next.

topics.title: The Greek world
topics.dateRangeLabel: Early Bronze Age Aegean to the Roman sack of Corinth
topics.summary: Greek history from the Bronze Age palaces until Rome came east (and stayed).

topics.title: Revolutions and political rupture
topics.summary: How governments get overthrown, and what people build in their place.

topics.title: Rome, from founding to fall
topics.summary: Rome grew from a village on the Tiber into an empire.

topics.title: Russian Revolution
topics.summary: The Russian Empire collapsed during the First World War, and revolutionaries fought over what came next.

topics.title: The American founders, one at a time
topics.summary: The men and women who made the United States, one life at a time, including several the statues leave out.

topics.title: Ancient cities, writing, and early states
topics.dateRangeLabel: Neolithic communities through early imperial societies
topics.summary: How cities, records, infrastructure, labor, and institutions changed what large communities could do.

topics.title: The assassins
topics.summary: The people who pulled the trigger or held the knife, and what they thought it would change.

topics.title: Before they were dictators
topics.summary: Where twentieth-century dictators came from, and what they were doing before anyone took them seriously.

topics.title: Byzantium
topics.summary: The eastern half of the Roman Empire outlived the West by almost a thousand years and never stopped calling itself Roman.

topics.title: Early Byzantium, 476–717
topics.summary: Justinian won back much of the old West, and his successors spent a century just trying to survive.

topics.title: Byzantium and the Crusades, 1081–1204
topics.summary: The Komnenos family rebuilds the empire and rides out the crusades. Their successors lose Constantinople to one.

topics.title: Late Byzantium, 1204–1453
topics.summary: After the crusaders took Constantinople, the Byzantines won it back and spent two centuries losing ground to the Ottomans.

topics.title: Middle Byzantium, 717–1081
topics.summary: The empire took three centuries to climb back to power under Basil II. His successors wasted it in fifty years.

topics.title: Composers' lives
topics.summary: The lives behind the music, from a medieval abbess to the women whose work went unplayed for decades.

topics.title: Conquerors
topics.summary: Empire builders from Macedon to Mongolia, and what happened to their empires once they were gone.

topics.title: Escaping slavery
topics.summary: People who freed themselves from slavery in the United States, and what several of them did with that freedom.

topics.title: Everyday lives in the past
topics.summary: What life was like for ordinary people, who did most of the work and left few records.

topics.title: Explorers who never came home
topics.summary: Expeditions whose leaders died on the way, from Magellan in the Philippines to Mallory on Everest.

topics.title: Forgotten lives
topics.summary: People who mattered in their own time and then dropped out of the story, from an Egyptian queen to a Hungarian baron.

topics.title: People you've never heard of who shaped France
topics.summary: France is usually told through its kings and generals. These people changed it from the side, and most are barely remembered.

topics.title: Impostors and pretenders
topics.summary: People who claimed to be someone else, sometimes a lost prince and sometimes just a doctor, and how far they got.

topics.title: Inventors and the fights over credit
topics.summary: The people behind everyday inventions, and the fights over patents, money, and credit that followed.

topics.title: Mad kings and what was really wrong with them
topics.summary: Rulers remembered as mad, and what historians now think was going on.

topics.title: The greatest discoveries in medicine
topics.summary: The people behind vaccines, anesthesia, insulin, and antibiotics, and the fights it took to get anyone to listen.

topics.title: Mexican Revolution
topics.summary: Mexico fought for ten years over who would run the country and who would own the land.

topics.title: Mongol Empire and Eurasian exchange
topics.summary: The Mongols built the largest land empire in history, and it brought distant parts of Eurasia into contact.

topics.title: Mothers of kings
topics.summary: Women who put their sons on thrones, and often kept a hand on the crown afterward.

topics.title: Painters' lives
topics.summary: The lives behind the paintings, including artists who were famous in their day and forgotten soon after.

topics.title: Paris Commune
topics.summary: After France lost to Prussia in 1871, Paris governed itself for two months until the army took it back.

topics.title: People who said no
topics.summary: People who refused to go along at the moment when going along was easiest.

topics.title: Philosophers' lives
topics.summary: The people behind the big ideas, and how much trouble those ideas got them into.

topics.title: Pioneers of flight
topics.summary: The people who got off the ground first, from paper balloons over France to the first person in orbit.

topics.title: Pirates
topics.summary: The real lives behind the legends, from Roman Britain to the South China Sea.

topics.title: Plague, disease, and society
topics.summary: How epidemics changed the places they hit, and how people behaved while they lasted.

topics.title: The power behind the throne
topics.summary: The ministers and advisers who really ran things, and what happened when their luck ran out.

topics.title: Quacks and miracle cures
topics.summary: Doctors, showmen, and true believers who sold cures that didn't work, and some that made people much worse.

topics.title: Queer lives before Stonewall
topics.summary: Lesbian, gay, and trans people who lived openly, or nearly so, in centuries that punished them for it.

topics.title: Royal favorites
topics.summary: The friends, lovers, and companions monarchs couldn't do without, and the courts that hated them for it.

topics.title: Saints, mystics, and heretics
topics.summary: Holy people the church honored, burned, or did both to, sometimes within a few decades of each other.

topics.title: Scientists who changed how we see the world
topics.summary: From a mathematician in Syracuse to the physicist who built the bomb, the people who redrew the universe.

topics.title: Spies
topics.summary: Four centuries of people who lied for a living, and what it cost them when the lie came apart.

topics.title: Legends of the Wild West
topics.summary: The outlaws, lawmen, and performers behind the Western, and how much of the legend they made up themselves.

topics.title: Scientists the textbooks left out
topics.summary: Women who did the work, from ancient Alexandria to the atomic age, and often watched someone else get the credit.

topics.title: Women who ruled
topics.summary: Queens, empresses, and one pharaoh who governed in their own right, usually against the wishes of the men around them.

topics.title: Writers' lives
topics.summary: The lives of writers people still read, from Elizabethan London to postwar Paris.

topics.title: Ancient Egypt
topics.summary: A long time ago, Egypt's kings built giant pyramids so everyone would remember them forever. It worked. People are still digging up their treasures, and one mummy even got its voice back.

topics.title: How animals live and talk
topics.summary: Animals are talking all the time. Wolves howl and whales sing, and scientists are slowly working out what they mean (some dogs are listening to you more closely than you think).

topics.title: Animals in history
topics.summary: History isn't only about kings and battles. A pig once nearly started a war, and a rhino won an election in Brazil (nobody asked the animals how they felt about any of it).

topics.title: Brains, feelings, and sleep
topics.summary: Your brain is squishy, and it runs absolutely everything you think and feel. Find out why the dark seems scarier than it really is, and what your brain gets up to while you're asleep.

topics.title: Bugs and other small creatures
topics.summary: There are far more insects than people, and honestly, they're running the place. Without them, a lot of plants and animals would be in serious trouble (so maybe be nice to the next ant you meet).

topics.title: Dinosaurs
topics.summary: Nobody has ever met a living dinosaur. So how do scientists know how big they got, or how they walked? They figure it out from bones and footprints, and sometimes from fossilized poop (really!).

topics.title: Where everyday things came from
topics.summary: Somebody had to invent the toilet. Somebody had to invent the weekend, too. These are the stories behind everyday things that nobody thinks twice about.

topics.title: Explorers
topics.summary: Some people just had to see what was on the other side of the ocean, or on top of the tallest mountain. So they packed up and went, even when nobody had drawn a map yet.

topics.title: Food and where it came from
topics.summary: Every snack has a story. Pizza took over the whole world, and ice cream once came in some very strange flavors (don't ask about the whale).

topics.title: Greek myths
topics.summary: The Greek gods were powerful and very easy to annoy. If you were a human in one of these stories, you needed to be clever, brave, or extremely lucky (preferably all three).

topics.title: How things work
topics.summary: Flip a switch and a light comes on. It seems like magic until you learn how it works, and then it's even better. These stops open up the machines you use every day.

topics.title: The human body
topics.summary: Your body runs a lot of machinery without asking your permission. It fights off germs while you sleep and fires sneezes across the room at alarming speed (gross, but impressive).

topics.title: Music and sound
topics.summary: Every time you whistle, you're shaking the air. Find out how instruments turn that shaking into music, and why some songs make you want to get up and dance.

topics.title: Life in the ocean
topics.summary: Most of the ocean is dark, cold, and very deep, and the animals down there have come up with some truly strange ways to live. One octopus even pulled off a heist.

topics.title: Plants, trees, and fungi
topics.summary: Plants can't run away from anything, so they've had to get creative. Some trap and eat insects, and ferns managed to outlast the dinosaurs without moving an inch.

topics.title: Volcanoes, earthquakes, and rocks
topics.summary: The ground feels solid, but it's moving right now, just very slowly. Every so often it moves very quickly instead, and that's when you get earthquakes and volcanoes.

topics.title: Scientists and inventors
topics.summary: Lots of big ideas started with someone asking a small question, like why things fall down. Meet the people who kept asking until they figured it out.

topics.title: Space
topics.summary: Space is very big and very far away, and people keep going there anyway. Find out how much the Moon weighs (a lot) and what robots are up to on Mars.

topics.title: Weather and wild skies
topics.summary: Weather is mostly warm air and cold air shoving each other around. Usually they're polite about it. Find out what happens inside a thunderstorm or a hurricane when they aren't, and how forecasters try to see it coming.

topics.title: Myths from around the world
topics.summary: Long before books, people all over the world told stories to explain how things came to be. Most of them agree that tricksters cause a lot of trouble. These come from Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas.
